held.title: Backfill aborts the migration if any AWS connector account has a NULL external_account_id
held.body: `assets_sources.external_account_id` is `NOT NULL`, but the backfill copies `a.external_account_id` from every AWS connector account without filtering NULLs. If `connector_accounts.external_account_id` is nullable, for example on an account created before its identity was resolved, one such row makes the INSERT fail and the whole migration fails at deploy. I can't see the `connector_accounts` schema, so I couldn't confirm the column is nullable. Fix: add `AND a.external_account_id IS NOT NULL` to the WHERE clause.

held.title: Backfill links and schedules sources for disabled or disconnected connector accounts
held.body:
The description says a source is made due only when an AWS account is created, enabled or reconnected. The backfill does not check whether the account is enabled or connected: it picks the most recently updated account per external ID, sets it as the link and sets `next_sync_at = NOW()`. This causes two problems:
- A disabled account becomes a due source, so the worker tries to sync it right away.
- If the newest row for an external ID is disabled and an older one is active, the source is linked to the disabled one.

I can't see whether `connector_accounts` has a status column or whether the worker skips such accounts. If it has one, filter on it or sort active accounts first in the `ORDER BY`.

held.title: The stale sweep makes a source due again while its original sync may still be running.
held.body:
`RecoverStale` marks any sync older than 15 minutes as FAILED and sets the source's `next_sync_at` to `now-1s`. Nothing stops the goroutine still running that sync. Because no sync for the source is RUNNING any more, `Claim` immediately starts a second one, so two workers list the same AWS account at once. When the first one finishes, `FinishIfRunning` updates no rows and `store` returns `errSyncNotRunning`. That rolls back every asset it gathered, and the attempt is counted toward the stale cap.

Trigger: a sync slower than `assetSyncStaleAfter`, for example many CloudFront pages under throttling with SDK retries. The source can then reach the 3-attempt cap and wait a day even though each run was making progress.

Fix: bound each sync with `context.WithTimeout(ctx, staleAfter)` inside `Process`, so a sync cannot outlive the sweep. Alternatively, have the sweep skip syncs whose worker is still alive, for example by tracking a heartbeat.
